newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent turns lower, rests on $18.65 support.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent turns lower, rests on $18.65 support.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures dipped on Thursday after a slightly firmer start, brokers said.
July Brent was down seven cents at $18.65 at 1107 GMT having peaked at $18.78 soon after the open.
"The market has not found strong support yet. But we don't expect a big move down today," said a broker
Other dealers said the market looked technically weak with support at $18.65 and $18.50 and some saw a soggy outlook for the physical market.
There was little fresh news after Wednesday's renewal of Iraq's oil-for-food deal.
U.S. gasoline demand has failed to lift the wider market this week and many expected the weight of other oil products in the West to soon pressure crude prices.
A bearish set of U.S. stock figures earlier this week added to downward pressure and dealers now await an outlook on world oil markets from the International Energy Agecy on Friday.
IPE gas oil was down $1.25 cents a tonne at $167.50 at 1105 GMT but analysts saw robust technical support in the area $160.00 to $165.00 a widely traded range in April.
Physical markets were also under pressure wtih Rotterdam barges talked under $1 a tonne above futures.
Dealers said German demand was poor and the Mediterranean market looked oversupplied.
